All four (rssp-s1, sstr-s1, daep-s1, ssdo-s1) are merged and DoD-complete as of this session. The operator then gave 5 pieces of UX feedback from their first full web-UI-driven feature completion, all captured to capture-log.md; 4 of the 5 (context-panel collapse, artefact drill-down browser, next-stage-action discoverability, plus the feature-summary-page item explicitly deferred out) were run through a full live /discovery -> /clarify -> approval cycle this session, producing the CURRENT active feature (2026-08-31-web-ui-navigation-legibility, Approved, ready for /benefit-metric). Immediately after approval, the operator reported two MORE production issues on the original af17f555 dogfooding journey (unrelated to anything above): (a) a test-plan session appearing to have 'reverted' from a completed DoR back to test-plan, and (b) an artefact count mismatch (3 vs 8) on /features/:slug. Both were investigated to a confirmed, evidenced root cause via direct log/code reading (browser automation to skills-framework.fly.dev was non-functional for most of this session -- auth kept bouncing back to the landing page even hitting /auth/github directly; investigation was done entirely via flyctl logs, flyctl machine status, and reading the actual route/adapter code instead). Root causes found: (a) computeStep1Summary's test-plan/definition-of-ready branches (src/web-ui/routes/skills.js, the ssp.1 Step-1-precompute mechanism) scan for a PER-STORY subdirectory convention (artefacts/[featureSlug]-tp-[storyId]/test-plan.md) that was never actually used -- the real artefacts are flat feature-level files (artefacts/[featureSlug]/test-plan.md), matching every other stage in the journey. The scanner never finds them, always reports 'no prior test-plan artefacts found', and the model redundantly re-generates test-plan content for the wrong story until the operator catches it. This is the mirror image of daep-s1 (a scanner missing a real file, vs. a parser not recognizing a real format). (b) listArtefacts (src/web-ui/adapters/artefact-list.js) checks the local git checkout on disk FIRST and returns immediately if it finds ANY artefacts there, never falling through to the more complete Postgres-backed store (pgArtefactRows) even when the local checkout is only PARTIALLY populated (stale relative to what's actually been produced mid-session, post-deploy). Neither fix was implemented this session -- both were deliberately captured and deferred per the operator's own explicit choice ('capture for now, stop here' for the test-plan/DoR convention question; the artefact-listing fix was queued but not reached before the newer report came in). A third, separate finding -- fly.toml's auto_stop_machines='suspend' / min_machines_running=0 causing the production machine to suspend after as little as ~6 minutes of idle time, confirmed via flyctl machine status event log cycling started<->suspended live during this investigation -- was identified as the most likely root cause of BOTH silent-hang incidents seen this session (an SSE turn opens, logs nothing further ever, no crash, no close event) and is a genuine beta-reliability risk distinct from anything code-fixable in this repo; this needs an operator infra/cost decision (disable auto-stop vs accept the tradeoff vs a suspend-aware mitigation), not a quick patch.
